Every CI run warns that the pinned actions/cache (v4.2.3) targets the deprecated Node.js 20 and is being forced onto Node.js 24

A person approved this proposal from the steward role. Carry the work out as an ordinary change.
Everything the proposal cites is copied below; nothing here points at a file you cannot open.

Proposal: 20261109-152554-x8b6 (key ci-actions-cache-pin-targets-deprecated-node20), queued at 2026-11-09T15:25:54.156042738Z by the steward role.
Rung of the requirements ladder: implementation.

## Source

path .github/workflows/ci.yml
```
# Athena's CI (docs/design/athena-v0.md §11.2): a thin call into Rust. Every job that builds starts with
# `./setup.sh --ci`. Actions are pinned by commit SHA, the token is read-only, and nothing is deployed. Tests
# that call real models are opt-in and never run here.
#
# Layout (docs/design/ci-routing.md §4.2). The old single `fmt, clippy, tests` job ran everything in sequence on
# one runner (about 16 minutes on a cold cache, docs/decisions.md D125; that earlier measurement is the only
# run time quoted here). The checks now run at the same time on separate runners:
#
#   gate ──► fmt ───────┐
#        ├─► clippy ────┼─► pass   (writes the D121 marker only if all three succeeded)
#        └─► test (6 shards, `xtask test-shard <k> 6`)
#   ci     needs gate, fmt, clippy, test; `if: always()`; the one check name that says whether a commit is green.
#
# The run time of this layout is NOT measured here; the throughput review measures it later. The
# `timeout-minutes` values are ceilings that stop a hung job, not measurements.
#
# Shards: `xtask test-shard <k> <n>` gives each workspace test target (every lib, bin, integration-test file,
# and one doctest unit per library) to exactly one shard. The test in xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs reads the
# matrix and the command below and fails unless the shards together cover every target exactly once. To
# change the shard count, change the matrix list and the `6` in the test command together.
#
# Cache layers (docs/design/ci-routing.md §4.1): toolchain, registry and target, keyed on the content of
# rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock. Every run restores them; only a push to the default branch saves them, so
# an unreviewed branch cannot fill or poison the shared entries. Each job reports exact, restore key or miss.
# Each of fmt, clippy and test has its own target key (target-fmt-, target-clippy-, target-test-) because they
# build different artifacts and would overwrite one another under one key. KNOWN EFFECT: the six test shards
# share one key and only shard 0 saves it, so the saved entry holds what shard 0 built; the other shards
# compile some of their packages cold. New keys also start cold, so the first runs after this change are
# slower. Both are for the throughput review to judge.
#
# Tool caches: gitleaks (path ~/.local/share/athena/tools/gitleaks) is keyed on runner OS and architecture and
# on athena.toml, where the pin lives. The athena binary (path ~/.local/share/athena/bin, with a stamp file
# `athena.inputs`) is keyed on runner OS and architecture and on hashFiles of exactly the nine globs that
# `cargo run -p xtask -- build-inputs` prints (BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS in xtask/src/main.rs): crates/**, xtask/**,
# rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md.
# That is every file the binary is compiled from, prompts and docs/system-facts.md included. Other files, such
# as CHANGELOG.md, README.md and the rest of docs/, are not in the key, so changing only those reuses the binary.
# There is no restore-keys fallback, so only an entry saved under an identical key is restored. A pull request
# that changes crates/ or xtask/ always misses the key (only the default branch saves) and rebuilds.
# `setup.sh --ci` also compares the stamp with a digest of the same globs and rebuilds on a mismatch. That skip
# applies only with --ci, and it runs before the dirty-tree refusal, which CI does not need because its checkout
# is clean; a local setup never skips. xtask/tests/policy.rs fails if a key misses a compiled-in file, differs
# from the xtask list, or a job restores after its setup step. Each tool cache is a restore step before the setup
# step in every job that runs it. fmt, clippy and test shard 0 save them, on the default branch only; history,
# attribution and pr-head restore only (the same keys are saved by the jobs above, and a pull-request job never
# saves). KNOWN EFFECT: a restored binary reports the source commit of the run that built it, not of the run that
# restored it; these jobs only run read-only checks. The time saved is not measured here; the throughput review
# measures it.
#
# Reuse of an earlier pass (docs/decisions.md D121): the `gate` job looks up `ci-pass-<governed fingerprint>`; a
# marker naming that fingerprint makes fmt, clippy and test skip (their `if`), and `ci` accepts that. The
# `pass` job needs all three, has no status override, and so runs only if every one succeeded; it alone writes
# and saves the marker, on pull-request branches too (entries stay on the branch that saved them). A failed
# shard therefore leaves no marker. KNOWN EFFECT: `ci` does not wait for `pass`, so a commit can show green a
# moment before its marker is saved.
name: ci

on:
  # Push runs only for main. A push to a pull request's branch ran the same checks a second time for the same
  # commit, in the push cache scope, which misses the pull_request run's cached pass. On PR #185 the pull_request
  # run passed from the cache in 26 s, while two push runs of the same commit each ran the full 16 minutes
  # (timings from the request; docs/decisions.md D125). The pull_request run satisfies the required check.
  # The exception is `athena/ci/**`: Athena pushes each job's candidate to `athena/ci/<job id>` and deletes the
  # branch when the job closes, so a push there is an Athena candidate CI run, not a pull request's branch.
  # Those runs are not on a pull request, and nothing reads their result yet.
  push:
    branches: [main, "athena/ci/**"]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    # Weekly, so that new gitleaks rules reach old commits, and so the default branch's cache entries stay fresh.
    - cron: "17 6 * * 1"

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Decides whether the earlier pass can be reused (D121). Runs once, so the fingerprint is built once.
  gate:
    name: gate (reuse of an earlier pass)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      skip:
```

### 2. path .github/workflows/pages.yml
```
# Publishes the explainer page to GitHub Pages (docs/design/explainer-site.md). A thin call into Rust:
# `cargo run -p xtask -- site` renders target/site/index.html from studies/firstmate-work-handling (and
# decisions.html from the records branch, fetched in the step before), and the
# three Pages actions upload and deploy that directory. The repository owner must set
# Settings -> Pages -> Source to "GitHub Actions" once; until then the deploy job fails.
name: pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deployment at a time; a newer push replaces one still waiting, but never cancels one in progress.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      # The checkout holds only main. The owner decision briefs page (decisions.html) reads the proposals from
      # the records branch, so fetch it into the local ref the renderer looks for. A failed fetch leaves the
      # branch missing, and the page then says so.
      - name: Fetch the records branch
        run: git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin +athena/records:refs/heads/athena/records || echo "::warning::the athena/records branch could not be fetched; decisions.html will list no proposals"
      - name: Render the page
        run: cargo run --locked -p xtask -- site
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: target/site

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

### 3. job 20261109-152932-19g0
Request:
```
Priority: low. GitHub run 42641502926, like other recent runs, warns on every cache step that actions/cache/restore and actions/cache/save at commit 5a3ec84e (v4.2.3) target Node.js 20, which is deprecated and now forced to run on Node.js 24. Move the actions/cache restore and save pins in .github/workflows/ci.yml to a full commit SHA of an actions/cache release that targets Node.js 24, with the version in a trailing comment, as the file already does. Pin the tag-only actions in .github/workflows/pages.yml (configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact, deploy-pages) by commit SHA too, to match. If the producer cannot confirm a release SHA from inside its working directory, it must stop and report that, not guess.

Acceptance:
- The change is made as described: Every CI run warns that the pinned actions/cache (v4.2.3) targets the deprecated Node.js 20 and is being forced onto Node.js 24
- No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass
- fmt, clippy and test pass

Files: actions/cache/restore, actions/cache/save, actions/cache, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/pages.yml
```
Outcome: none recorded yet.
